title: Enforce a sliding-window limit
statement:
Step 5 · Caching and admission

A sliding-window limiter counts accepted requests in (now − duration, now]. The lower boundary is excluded. Recording rejected requests would create a different policy.

Build it

Return an allow/deny result per nondecreasing timestamp. Keep at most limit accepted requests within the window. duration is positive; limit is nonnegative.

Contract: Implement window using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: times = [0, 0.1, 0.2, 1, 1.1], duration = 1, limit = 2
Expected: [true, true, false, true, true]
Input: times = [0, 0, 0], duration = 5, limit = 0
Expected: [false, false, false]
Hint

Expire timestamps at or before now−duration before deciding whether to admit the next request.

Review your understanding

Compare token-bucket bursts, fixed-window boundary spikes, and sliding-window storage costs.

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
